dispositions.statement: The 9 flagged rows in these 7 quarters are floating loans whose whole margin is printed as PIK, with the benchmark in the Index column and the coupon in the rate column: Masco subordinated debt 'EURIBOR 10.00 % PIK 13.25 %' (2024-12-31 to 2025-09-30) and Cube's sterling delayed draw 'SONIA 10.00 % PIK' 14.22 / 14.10 / 13.73 (2025-06-30 to 2026-06-30). Par grows by about half the coupon each half-year, not by the margin: Masco EUR 5,000 to 5,331 (5,000 x (1 + 13.25 pct / 2) = 5,331.25) and 5,666 at 2025-12-31; Cube GBP 2,040 to 2,185 (+7.1 pct, 14.10 / 2 = 7.05) and 2,185 to 2,334 (+6.8 pct, 13.73 / 2 = 6.87). So the whole coupon is paid in kind and, under the owner's D-232 reading, the build publishes pik_rate = the printed coupon, basis_spread = the margin, coupon type floating and interest_rate_cash 0 (row corrections, rfbn loop). The rule reads the margin printed before 'PIK' as the PIK rate and flags the difference. Its D-232 repair accepts the coupon only when the margin follows '<benchmark> +', and this filer prints the benchmark in its own cell with no '+' (REQ-rfbn-1). A rule problem, not a data error. CAVEAT for REQ-rfbn-1: the printed format alone is not enough. Cube's dollar delayed draw at 2025-09-30 prints the same form ('SOFR 7.44 % PIK 11.44 %'), but its PIK tag is 7.44 and the same filing's other Cube dollar line prints 3.00 cash + 4.44 PIK. The whole-coupon reading was withdrawn there in round 2 (D-238), and that row now publishes pik 7.44 as printed. A format-only repair of the rule would have accepted the contradicted pik 11.44 without a word. The repair should also require par growth of about the coupon over a period (or another check independent of the format), and this proposal covers only the 9 rows that have it.
